crisis_power_cut_arrive.text: Pressure fine, oxygen fine. Lovely quiet afternoon, {called}. Somebody remind me never to say that out loud.
The electrician says the wiring is 'mostly fine'. Mostly. I've put the emergency kit on the trolley anyway.
And the generator was 'serviced' last month. By the same man who services the canteen's toaster.
crisis_power_cut_arrive.head: tilt

then.text: Generator's steady. You kept your head, {called}. Half the hospital didn't even keep its lights.
I'm writing 'excellent' in the incident form. They'll think it's sarcasm. It isn't.
then.head: nod

else.text: We got through it. Next time, think first about who is breathing for the patient. Everything else comes after.
Incident form tonight. I'll write it kindly. Kindly-ish.
else.head: down

crisis_power_cut_after.text: And that headlamp gets checked every Monday from now on. By me. Personally. Forever.

crisis_ramesh_arrive.text: Theatre's on the phone asking for 'Ramesh Kumar'. Just that. As if that narrows it down in India.
Bed 3 and Bed 5, both Ramesh Kumar, both in their fifties, both fasting and grumpy, both answer to 'uncle'.
One gallbladder is coming out today. Only one. Check properly, Doctor.

then.text: Right man on the trolley. Theatre said thank you, which they have never said before. I've written down the date.

else.text: I've re-checked the bands myself. Next time we check before the porter arrives, not after, na?

crisis_ramesh_after.text: And somebody give the other Ramesh his breakfast. He's been staring at my tiffin for an hour.
crisis_ramesh_after.head: tilt

crisis_crowd_arrive.text: Where is the doctor? Somebody answer us!
Doctor, the patient passed away. The family is here, and so is half the colony. Breathe first. Then we talk.
crisis_crowd_arrive.head: down

then.text: Thank you for telling us properly. Nobody else did.
then.head: nod

then.text: They've gone down with the forms. That's as good as this day was ever going to get, Doctor.
then.head: nod

else.text: Security walked them down. It'll be in tomorrow's paper, hopefully with a photo of the wrong doctor.
else.head: down

crisis_crowd_after.text: Sit for two minutes. I've put tea on the desk. Don't argue with me.

crisis_donors_arrive.text: The blood bank has nothing in the patient's group, Doctor. Nothing. The fridge is basically a cupboard.
So the whole family has lined up outside to donate. One uncle came straight from a wedding, by the smell of it.
Everyone says they're perfectly healthy. Everyone always says that.
crisis_donors_arrive.head: tilt

then.text: Units cross-matched and running. The pressure's coming up, and the family is very proud of itself.
then.head: nod

else.text: The blood bank sent units back, Doctor. We lost time we didn't have. Donor rules before needles, please.

crisis_donors_after.text: Now the uncle wants to know if he can donate after the next wedding. I said no. Firmly.

crisis_insurance_arrive.text: Doctor, the insurance company has sent the form back. With comments. In red ink.
Every rejected claim is money this hospital has already spent. I would like it back. So would my blood pressure.

then.text: Clean form, honest answers. The TPA officer called it 'unusually correct'. I've never been so moved by paperwork.

else.text: The claim is in trouble, Doctor. I'll speak to the TPA. Meanwhile, please learn waiting periods. Please.
else.head: shake

crisis_insurance_after.text: Also, the family thanked us. Nobody thanks the insurance desk. I'm a little emotional. Tell no one.
crisis_insurance_after.head: down

crisis_snakebite_arrive.text: Snakebite! Two hours on a tempo from the village, and the whole family came along.
One cousin brought a dead snake in a plastic bag. Nobody's sure it's the one that bit.
The twenty-minute clotting test is done. The card's on the trolley. Read it before the family tells you their theory.
crisis_snakebite_arrive.head: nod

then.text: Stable. Antivenom logged, family calmed, and the dead snake has been asked to leave the building.
then.head: nod

else.text: We sorted it, with the registrar shouting down the phone. The snakebite protocol is on the wall, Doctor. In big letters.

crisis_snakebite_after.text: The grandmother says she'll bring sweets every year. Last year's snakebite family still does.
crisis_snakebite_after.head: tilt

crisis_dengue_arrive.text: Dengue season, {called}. Every bed has a fever, every family has a platelet count, and every count is on WhatsApp.
Two units of platelets. That's all, till tomorrow. Platelets aren't sweets. We don't give them to whoever shouts loudest.

then.text: Good. The ones in danger got fluids, the low counts got platelets, and the rest got paracetamol and a lecture.
then.head: nod

else.text: Look again at who was in shock. The count is the loudest number on the sheet, not the most important one.

crisis_dengue_after.text: And tell the families: papaya leaves make a lovely salad. They are not a treatment.

crisis_inspection_arrive.text: The inspectors are in the car park, Doctor. Mr. Malhotra is already sweating through his good shirt.
I've made a list of everything that's wrong. It's long. We can't do all of it, so we do what matters.

then.text: Passed! The inspector wrote 'well-organised ward'. Mr. Malhotra wants it on a banner outside.

else.text: Remarks, Doctor. Several. We'll fix them by next week. Honestly, this time.
else.head: down

crisis_inspection_after.text: And will somebody please paint that damp patch. It's been there since the day I joined.
crisis_inspection_after.head: tilt
